newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. council unlikely to soon act on Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. council unlikely to soon act on Swiss banks.

text.p: The New York City Council Speaker Tuesday met with Swiss officials about a proposed bill to force Swiss banks to settle with Holocaust victims but Swiss officials said he told them no swift action was planned.
"What I learned is that this is just the beginning of the whole process," Lily Nabholz told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Nabholz is a member of the Swiss House of Representatives and heads the committee on legal affairs that wrote a decree lifting the country's secrecy laws. This has aided probes into the controversy over whether Swiss banks kept millions of dollars deposited in secret accounts by Jews before and during the Second World War.

The Swiss representative, who was accompanied at the meeting by Alfred Dfago, the Swiss Ambassador Designate to the U.S., added New York City was the only local U.S. government that had contacted her about such a bill and said she hoped the issue were resolved before the council acted.
Nabholz added New York City's role as a leading financial center underscores the importance of the council's decision.

The New York City Council last week proposed a bill that would stop the city from depositing money in Swiss banks until the Swiss government set up a compensation fund for Holocaust victims. The council speaker also proposed harsher measures, including having the city sell shares of three Swiss banks owned by its pension funds if the Swiss government does not reach a satisfactory settlement with Jewish Holocaust victims.

A spokeswoman for Speaker Peter Vallone said that he told the two Swiss officials he met that while the council has set a hearing on the issue for February 10, it would be highly unusual for it to approve a bill on the same day.
"There might be another hearing scheduled," added Bernice Spitzer, explaining this would depend in part on what information was learned from the first forum.

New York State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver plans to hold a hearing on February 13 to determine "under what circumstances may a foreign bank's license or certification be revoked." And Gov George Pataki has said he was reviewing proposals to curb the activities of Swiss banks.
The moves marked the first entry by the state and local governments into the controversy.
